title: Reduced affine flat model with geometrically reduced generic fibre after radicial base change
statement: Let $X$ be affine and $f:X\to T$ locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with image in an affine open $V\subseteq T$. Let $\eta$ be a generic point of $T$ and suppose $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There are an open $U\subseteq T$ containing $\eta$, integral affine $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], reduced affine $Y$, a universal homeomorphism $q:S\to U$, and a flat locally finitely presented map $g:Y\to S$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There is a generic point $\eta\prime$ of $S$ with $q(\eta\prime)=\eta$ and geometrically reduced $Y_{\eta\prime}$. For every $s\in S$, $Y_s$ is geometrically irreducible if and only if $X_{q(s)}$ is geometrically irreducible. Here $q(s)$ is regarded as a point of $T$ via $U\hookrightarrow T$. No assertion that any nongeneric fibre is irreducible is made.

proof.text: Use radicial generic-reduced preparation to obtain an affine open of the original base, an integral affine radicial base model, and a reduced affine locally finite type source. Retain the generic point, geometrically reduced generic fibre, and pointwise comparison of geometric irreducibility. This step does not assert flatness or finite presentation.

The affine source map to the affine integral model base is quasi-compact. Apply generic flat finite presentation, obtaining a nonempty open W. The generic point lies in W by its generic-point property.

The base universal homeomorphism maps W to an open. Choose a principal open B in its image containing the image of the generic point. Its inverse image A lies in W by injectivity of the homeomorphism. Restrict both base model and family to A, and identify B with its open image in the original base. Affine morphisms preserve affine opens under preimage, integral schemes restrict to nonempty integral opens, and reduced schemes restrict to reduced opens. Transfer flatness and local finite presentation from W to A using the restriction-of-restriction arrow isomorphism. Universal homeomorphisms are stable under base change and composition with isomorphisms.

The generic point regarded in A stays generic, since an open embedding induces the specialization relation. The square defining the restricted family gives a pullback square on each residue-field fibre. The base open immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields, hence the fibre square is an arrow isomorphism. Geometric reducedness and irreducibility respect this isomorphism. Combine the latter equivalence with the preparation comparison and the equality of the composite base maps.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_generic_radicial_geometrically_reduced_model
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (V : T.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (himage : Set.range f ⊆ V)
    (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ (U : T.Opens), η ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (S Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : S ⟶ U.toScheme) (g : Y ⟶ S),
        IsAffine S ∧ IsIntegral S ∧ IsAffine Y ∧ IsReduced Y ∧
        IsUniversalHomeomorphism q ∧ Flat g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g ∧
        ∃ η' : S, IsGenericPoint η' Set.univ ∧ (q ≫ U.ι) η' = η ∧
          GeometricallyReduced (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η') ∧
          ∀ s : S, GeometricallyIrreducible (g.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ↔
            GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField ((q ≫ U.ι) s))
